newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cosipa stops talks with Santos unions.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cosipa stops talks with Santos unions.

text.p: Brazilian steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) has broken off talks with unions at Santos port and will use only its own workers at its private terminal from August 4, it said in a statement.

"After 14 meetings and in light of the failure to respect what was signed at the last meeting between Cosipa's negotiating commission and portworker union representatives, the company has decided not to accept extending negotiations," it said.

Cosipa has been in talks with unions since April, when stevedores staged two strikes at Santos in protest against the steel firm's decision to use its own workers to load and unload at its own terminal.
"The agreement to share the work in the firm's port will only be valid until August 3," Cosipa said, referring to an interim solution agreed on after the strikes.
Union officials were not immediately available to comment on Cosipa's decision.
